deviations.why: Measured 8 vs 16 vs 32 on this pair: 32 gave about twice the aggregate throughput at 24 concurrent (222.5 vs 107.4 tok/s) and half the tail latency (10.4s vs 21.4s), for 2.5% less KV cache and no change to single-stream speed. Upstream's 8 is a single-user default.
auto resolves to 1048576 on this checkpoint, which does not fit on two GB10s.
The mod is opt-in and only serves speculative decoding, which is off here. The stock loader in this image is already correct for the checkpoint.

Measured 1.4-2.8x single stream, but KV cache falls 681,894 to 420,192 tokens, concurrency 2.60x to 1.60x and load 150s to 195s, and the gains shrink under load. Kept as a documented per-deployment override for single-user boxes rather than a shared-server default.

64 is what vLLM picks for itself here: with the flag absent it uses max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens) * 2, which is 32 * 1 * 2 at our settings (config/vllm.py). Upstream's 48 is a reduction from their own default of 96, which is 8 * 6 * 2 at max_num_seqs 8 with 5 draft tokens. Kept explicit so the value the measurements were taken at is recorded rather than inferred.

deviations.upstream: {reasoning_parser: deepseek_v4, empty start and end strings}
deviations.why: vLLM builds this itself. With --reasoning-parser set and no --reasoning-config, _set_default_reasoning_config_args creates ReasoningConfig(reasoning_parser=...), and its reasoning_start_str and reasoning_end_str already default to the empty strings upstream spells out, so passing it changes nothing.

The deepseek_v4 renderer enables thinking when neither thinking nor enable_thinking is passed (tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py), so the flag restates the default. Leaving it off also lets a client turn thinking off per request instead of having it forced server-side.
The same renderer sets reasoning_effort to high whenever thinking is enabled and no string is supplied, so upstream's value is already what we serve.

verified.smoke: 17*19 -> 323; 27.6 tok/s single stream, 222.5 tok/s aggregate at 24 concurrent
notes: Launch worker rank 1 headless BEFORE head rank 0.
attention-backend is B12X; vllm-project/recipes says B12X_MLA_SPARSE, which this image rejects at startup.
Needs both RoCE twins via NCCL_IB_HCA and a routable DAC subnet; NetworkManager must own the addresses or they vanish.

Per-token KV cost falls as context rises (CSA/HCA sparse attention): 32K gave 99,949 tokens, 64K gave 196,022 and 256K gave 675,260 for the same ~19 GiB. A linear KV estimator is badly wrong for deepseek_v4.
Aggregate throughput looking flat past the seqs limit means requests are queueing, not that the GPU is saturated; the tell is tail latency diverging from p50.

6 is not a multiple of the checkpoint's dspark_block_size 5, so upstream's value is rejected at boot. Measured here at 5: single stream 30 to 34 tok/s on prose, 42 on code and 84 on counting, and TTFT unchanged, but KV falls 671,756 to 406,755 tokens and aggregate throughput at 24 concurrent falls 206.9 to 158.0 tok/s with the tail 11.1s to 14.6s. A shared server pays for one user's speedup, so it is left off.

verified.smoke: corn.jpeg -> "Corn on the cob."; 28.1 tok/s single stream, 238.8 tok/s at 24 concurrent
notes: Runs on the same image as the text recipe; the checkpoint declares architectures DeepseekV4ForCausalLM but this image auto-resolves DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration, so no --hf-overrides is needed.
Do not pass --enforce-eager. CUDA graphs capture fine and eager costs about 7x decode speed.
temperature 0 makes the model loop in reasoning and never emit content. Send temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95, which is what DeepSeek evaluated; generation_config.json disagrees at top_p 1.0.
An image costs at most 387 prompt tokens (vision_max_n_token 384 plus compressor pad), measured 404 with text for a 207 KB photo. Long multi-image prompts are untested here.
Model is experimental and vLLM vision support is unmerged (vllm-project/vllm#54566).

deviations.why: The spill tier keeps prompt states on disk, so long agent conversations come back after a restart without a new prefill. 128 GiB a Spark is what the deployment ran with.

Renders the reasoning-effort line at the prompt's tail, so switching effort or thinking keeps the kept-prompt cache warm (issue #93). The serving deployment ran with it on; upstream leaves it off until the effort levels are checked.
At most 2 kept states for one conversation, the author's value, so one long chat cannot fill the cache's entries alone. The serving deployment ran with it.
TensorFold checks no API key, so rank 0 listens on loopback and a proxy that checks one serves the network.
The proxy in front holds 8888.
